headline: Advanced police vehicle and camera projects, Pershing Way pump station roof work, and a 2026-2029 Westbrook General Unit contract; adopted Lincoln Street sidewalk changes.
summary: The council adopted orders on a car show permit, Lincoln Street sidewalk and roadway work, public safety building lighting, and grant funds. It passed first readings on a replacement police vehicle, police cameras, a pump station roof, a plate compactor, and a labor contract. It also approved the hours and voting place for the November 3, 2026 election.
decisions: Approved the July 20 and August 3, 2026 meeting minutes; no objections were received.
Adopted Orders 2026-89 and 2026-90 on second and final reading, covering replacement pump station doors and a forestry mulcher rental (vote 6-0-1).
Adopted Resolve 2026-16 setting voter registration hours and the voting place for the November 3, 2026 state general election (vote 6-0-1).
Approved a mass gathering permit for the Hot Rods & Heroes Car Show (vote 6-0-1).
Approved a Recreation & Conservation Commission expenditure for the Presumpscot Regional Land Trust 2026 Summer Trail Challenge (vote 6-0-1).
Adopted an amendment to Order 2026-52 on LED lighting upgrades at the Public Safety Building (vote 6-0-1).
Adopted an amendment to Order 2025-81 on Lincoln Street sidewalk and roadway improvements (vote 6-0-1).
Adopted an amendment to Order 2025-171 on Maine Bureau of Highway Safety impaired driving enforcement grant funds (vote 6-0-1).
Approved the first reading of Order 2026-96 on federal asset forfeiture funds after removing "& Expenditure" from its title (vote 6-0-1).
Approved the first reading of Order 2026-97 confirming an emergency expenditure for a replacement police vehicle (vote 6-0-1).
Approved the first reading of Order 2026-98 accepting and spending an Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (vote 6-0-1).
Approved the first reading of Order 2026-99 authorizing an agreement for the Police Department camera replacement project (vote 6-0-1).
Approved the first reading of Order 2026-100 authorizing an expenditure for the Pershing Way pump station roof replacement (vote 6-0-1).
Approved the first reading of Order 2026-101 authorizing purchase of a vibratory plate compactor for Public Services (vote 6-0).
Approved the first reading of Order 2026-102 approving the 2026-2029 collective bargaining agreement with the Westbrook General Unit (vote 6-0-1).

WESTBROOK CITY COUNCIL 
REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 
MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 14, 2026 AT 6:00 PM  
WESTBROOK HIGH SCHOOL (ROOM 114) 
125 STROUDWATER ST.  
 
 
 
  
I. LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT 
Meeting called to order at 6:00pm by City Council President Jennifer Munro. City Clerk Ellis Ledoux read the 
City Council Land Acknowledgment statement into the record. 
 
  
II. ROLL CALL 
City Councilors Present: Michael Shaughnessy (At-Large, Vice-President), Brian McCambridge (Ward 1)(via 
Zoom), Anna A. Turcotte (Ward 3), Victor Chau (Ward 2), Amy Faulkingham (Ward 4), Jennifer Munro (Ward 5, 
President) 
 
City Councilors Absent: Gary Raidon (At-Large) 
 
Other City Officials Present:  Eric Dudley (Director of Engineering & Public Services), Jennie Franceschi 
(Assistant City Administrator), Greg Hamilton (Director of Emergency Communications & IT), Angela Holmes 
(City Administrator), Sean Lally (Police Chief), Ellis Ledoux (City Clerk), Joanne LePauloue (Director of Human 
Resources), David Morse (Mayor), Monique Cornett (Director of Economic Development), Rebecca Spitella 
(Director of Code Enforcement & Planning) 
 
  
III. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 
City Council President Munro led all present in the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
  
IV. APPROVAL OF MINUTES  
 
 July 20, 2026 - Committee of the Whole & Special City Council Meeting  
August 3, 2026 - Regular City Council Meeting & Facilities & Streets Committee Meeting 
 City Council President Munro stated that unless any objections were received, the minutes would 
stand as presented. No objections received.  
 
  
V. MAYOR'S MESSAGE 
Mayor Morse read his message into the record. A summary is included below: 
• Written comments for public comment should be received by 10am on the day of the meeting to 
ensure inclusion in to public comment section of the meeting  
• A change to public comment requirements will now ask residents to disclose only whether they are a 
resident of Westbrook but not their home address.  
• Exciting update about METRO student transit bus pass program  
• Mayor Morse wanted to reflect on the passing of Dolly Parton.
VI. CITY COUNCIL MESSAGES 
Councilor Faulkingham shared that there is a resident who shared concerns about where the bus stop would be 
for their young child and she wanted to offer thanks to both the School transportation staff and to the Police 
Department for their timely response.  
 
Councilor Munro shared that the Westbrook Education Foundation is doing their first fundraiser this coming 
weekend.  
 
 
  
VII. STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE UPDATE 
There was no Student Representative update. 
 
  
VIII. PUBLIC COMMENT 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for the first public comment portion of this meeting. The 
following individuals spoke: Stephanie Anderson (Cape Elizabeth Resident, Running for DA for Cumberland 
County), Joseph Chawes (Westbrook Resident, via Zoom),Councilor Turcotte
